Early signs of AI-driven productivity growth in the information sector?Posted on October 22, 2026

SHARE THIS PAGE:

Link Copied

The takeaway
Since the advent of GenAI, labor productivity in the information sector has grown much faster than usual and much faster than in the overall economy.
Tracking labor productivity growth
Labor productivity is a measure of how much output each worker produces. Our FRED graph above shows real output per worker in the information sector (blue line), which includes publishing, broadcasting, telecommunications, and data processing/data centers. It also shows output per worker in the economy as a whole (red line).
The data start, purposefully, in the first quarter of 2024, when generative AI tools such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Google’s Gemini, Microsoft’s Copilot, and Anthropic’s Claude were rapidly gaining mainstream use.
Recently, labor productivity in the information sector has grown faster than usual and considerably faster than in the economy as a whole. For example, from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026, information sector labor productivity grew by 13.70% while aggregate labor productivity grew by 2.17%.
In the past, information sector labor productivity has typically been higher than aggregate labor productivity, but not to this extent. For example, from 2010 to 2026 (not shown in the graph), information sector labor productivity grew at an average annual rate of 7.68% while aggregate labor productivity grew at 1.22%.
Interpretation
It seems possible that we're seeing early signs of AI-driven productivity gains in the information sector. While the information sector accounts for only a small fraction of total employment (1.8%), it has generally been an important contributor to aggregate economic growth because of its strong productivity growth.
Data details
Both series are normalized to start at 1, and the natural logarithm (log) is applied to the resulting series to make the data’s path easier to visualize. If a series grows at a constant rate, its log exhibits a linear trend, with the slope corresponding to the growth rate.
How this graph was created: In FRED, search for and select “Real Value Added by Industry: Information.” Click on “Edit Graph,” scroll to “Customize data,” and add the series “All Employees, Information.” In the “Formula” section, insert (a/b)/(0.58492). (The 0.58492 is the value in the base period, Q1 2024). Under “Units,” select “Natural Log.” Use the “Add Line” tab to search for and select “Real Gross Domestic Product.” In the “Customize data” section, add the series “Employment Level,” add the formula (a/b)/(0.14338), and select “Natural Log” under “Units.” In the “Format” tab, select “Customize” under Line 2 and change “Line style” to “Solid” and “Color” to “#85103d.”. Finally, change the start date of the graph to “2023-12-01.”
Suggested by Oksana Leukhina and Gus Gerlach.
